hazards.evidence: Frequently used items (dishes, cups, bowls) are stored on high shelves above counter height.
Some dishes and bowls are stored in lower cabinets, but accessing them may require bending, which could be difficult post-surgery.
The floor appears to be hardwood, which can be slippery, especially without a rug or mat near the sink area.
There is no visible rug, but the transition between rooms and the hardwood floor itself could pose a slipping hazard.
An electrical cord is visible on the floor, posing a tripping hazard.
There appears to be a slight level change or step-down between the kitchen and adjacent room, which is not clearly marked.
